title: Vercel Moved Who Pays for Your Agent
caption:
I almost wired a side project to my own Claude plan this week.

On September 14 Vercel shipped native subscription auth for the AI SDK harness layer. Nine adapters, no code change, no new settings — your app can authenticate through the coding-agent subscription already signed in on the host instead of an API key. Tempting when you're solo and watching every dollar.

Then I read Anthropic's own docs. Pro and Max limits are shared across Claude and Claude Code, so a background job spends the capacity you wanted that afternoon. And third-party developers aren't allowed to offer claude.ai login or rate limits in their products without prior approval. So this is for your machine, not your customers.

Also worth knowing: if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is sitting in your environment, none of it fires and you're on metered API rates anyway.

Would you bill your own plan?

slides.headline:
Vercel Just
Moved Who Pays
slides.sub: September 14. The AI SDK harness layer can authenticate a coding agent through the subscription already signed in on your host. No API key, no code change.

slides.title: Nine Adapters
slides.sub: Claude Code, Cline, Codex, Cursor, fx, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, OpenCode and Pi — wherever the harness itself supports subscription login.

slides.title:
Three Modes.
Three Payers.
items: ai-gateway — Gateway credits or the Vercel invoice. Never reads a subscription.
direct — an explicit provider key wins. Otherwise the plan allowance pays.
auto (default) — same as direct, when no AI Gateway credentials are set.

slides.headline:
One Env Var
Moves The Bill
slides.sub: Anthropic’s own docs: with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set, Claude Code authenticates with the key instead of your subscription — API charges, not included usage.

slides.headline:
Same Limit As
Your Terminal
slides.sub: Pro and Max usage limits are shared across Claude and Claude Code. A background job spends the capacity you wanted at 4pm.

slides.headline:
Not For Your
Customers
slides.sub: Anthropic does not allow third-party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits in their products without prior approval. This is host-bound.
